issues.reason: Compound concepts makes the head genus mandatory ("The genus itself is ALWAYS emitted either way"; a solid/hyphenated transparent modifier+head "always emit the genus"), and `(Inheritance sky_cat cat)` appears nowhere in the parse even though cliff_spire, nightmoth, cold_snap, mist_light and feather_harvest all carry theirs.

`(Member sk_crowd_1 crowd) (GroupOf sk_crowd_1 nightmoth)` is the singular "a flock of birds" pattern applied to the plural "crowds of nightmoths", asserting one crowd where the text states several — number is read off the surface ("emit the one the surface shows").

One `sk_gather_1` cannot occur on six disjoint nights, so a single Past event witness carrying `(Time sk_gather_1 sk_nights_2)` misstates the content (and the Time filler is a group entity, not a calendar term, deictic or day-part symbol); the knock-on is real — plural "the hunts" resolves to the one `sk_hunt_1` at line 79.

Cardinality is stated to take `a native integer` and ParticleFromNormal is licensed only as a Measure magnitude or an approximate clock value, so the distribution in the count slot is ill-typed and breaks the `Compute` hard-integer counting machinery.

The half that stands: `night` is a day-part slot symbol, not a period unit, so `(Every e 1 night)` mis-slots it where the stated recipe gives the slot atom `(Time e night)` plus the cycle `(Every e 1 day)` (mirroring morning -> day); the half that does not: "per night" here quantifies the OBJECT count (thirty moths a night), not the counting event's period, so the reviewer's prescribed pair would not capture it either — which is the reviewer's own fourth gap.

Hunting neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes the nightmoths (success is not entailed), and the instruction set's explicit fallback is "When the test is unclear, default to Theme", so `Patient` violates the stated role test and breaks statement/question role agreement.

The dependent-existential doctrine makes an object under a universal a per-binding Skolem term unless "the same Y" / "a certain Y" cues the shared reading, so reusing the constants `sk_fuel_1` and `sk_mistlight_1` inside the per-member rules asserts one shared portion of mire-essence and one shared mist-light across the three stations — more than the text states.

The deviation is real — the convention is `sk_<class>_<n>` and "fuel" is neither the class nor a word the text uses — but a witness symbol is an opaque identifier typed by `(Member sk_fuel_1 mire_essence)`, so nothing false or ill-typed enters the KB and this alone would not defect the parse.

gaps_confirmed: A hedged numeral count ("about thirty nightmoths"): Cardinality takes a native integer, CardinalityPhrase covers only numberless vague phrases, and CardinalityAtLeast/AtMost only bounds — no licensed carrier.

An event distributed over a counted set of calendar units ("on six of the next ten nights"): days are stated to be terms, not entities, so there is no partitive over nights and Time has no slot for a set of occasions.
A forward-looking window relative to the narrative present ("the next ten nights"): the anaphoric-time rules cover only a single "that / the following <unit>" increment from an antecedent.
A per-unit rate on a counted object ("about thirty nightmoths per night"): compound rate units belong to Measure, while Every / TimesPer quantify the event's recurrence, not an object group's count.
An ordinal's stated domain restriction ("the first cold snap of Year 2"): `(Ordinal <entity> <n> <scale>)` has no slot for the domain the ranking is relative to.
new_gaps: A bare plural of collectives whose member kind is stated ("crowds of nightmoths"): the `(Member g flock) (GroupOf g bird)` pattern is singular-only, and no form is stated for a group whose members are themselves groups.

A mass / bare-substance object under a universal ("the three stations burned extra mire-essence"): the dependent-existential machinery is spelled out for indefinite COUNT objects (`(sk_book $x)`), leaving it unstated whether a per-member mass portion is minted the same way.
defect_summary: Index 0: emit the mandatory compound genus `(Inheritance sky_cat cat)` beside `(GroupOf sk_skycats_1 sky_cat)`. Index 1: "crowds of nightmoths" takes a group OF CROWDS — `(GroupOf sk_crowds_1 crowd)` as the attract event's Theme, each member's nightmoth membership handed down by a per-member rule — not one crowd witness. Index 2: NO licensed form exists — Time admits only calendar terms, deictics and day-part symbols and the instruction set states days are terms rather than entities, so an event recurring on a counted subset of nights cannot be encoded; the compliant behaviour is to leave the six-nights restriction (and the single collapsed event) out and record the gap, which is filed above. Index 3: NO licensed form — the compliant behaviour is to omit the hedged count atom entirely and record the gap. Index 5: `(Theme sk_hunt_1 sk_nightmoths_2)`, and `(Theme (sk_hunt $x) ...)` in the per-member rule. Index 6: give each station its own portion — `(Patient (sk_burn $x) (sk_mire_essence $x))` with `(Member (sk_mire_essence $x) mire_essence)` as a rule conjunct, and likewise a per-binding mist-light in the produce rule.
notes: The reviewer filed "the first cold snap OF YEAR 2" only as a gap, but dropping the domain restriction also widens the claim to first-ever, which Core patterns bars ("carry it, or leave the whole claim out") — a second defect route to the same conclusion. Everything else in the passage is compliant: the every-lantern rule with its `On` premise, the strength-0 no-lantern rule with its "no" companion, the collective gather with no per-member rule, and the `(BeforeBy sk_fall_1 sk_strong_1 1 month)` fallback for "the following month" all follow the stated forms.
